by_behaviour: Already pays for a sleep app
why_not: Free YouTube with a 30-minute timer already does the job for me, and I've never paid for a sleep app. Since the trial has no auto-charge I might try it out of curiosity, but I don't see myself paying 4,900 won a month for slightly smarter fading.
YouTube with a 30-minute timer already works for me and costs nothing. I might try the free 14 days since there's no auto-charge, but I can't see myself paying for something I've always gotten free.

I'd probably start the free 14-day trial since nothing bills automatically, but I'm cutting subscriptions right now. With earphones in, the fade-out and the button to resume are nice-to-haves, and the free version's 30-minute timer already does most of that for me.

No auto-charge on the trial is nice, so I'd actually start the 14 days without worrying about forgetting to cancel. But on $9,000 a year, even 3,250 won a month for something YouTube sleep music already does for free is hard to justify, so I'd most likely stop at the free version.

I'd probably install the free 14-day trial since there's no auto-charge, but I wouldn't pay yet. A brand-new app with no ratings, guessing when I fell asleep from my phone lying next to me while I've got earphones in, isn't proof I'd trust. It's the app grading its own homework.

I'd probably start the free 14-day trial since there's no auto-billing, but I wouldn't pay yet. The app is grading itself with a phone on my nightstand, and with my bedtime moving every week, 7 nights per method feels too noisy to trust, so on $28k I'd just stay on the free version and my YouTube sleep sounds.

No auto-charge on the trial is nice, so I'd probably try the 14 days for free, but my AirPods already stop the sound when I fall asleep and a free YouTube playlist does the rest. When the trial ends I'd just not pay, like I do with every trial.

I'd probably download it for the free 14 days since there's no auto-charge and the auto-replay is off by default, which is what I worry about. But I already play YouTube rain sounds for free with a timer, and I've tried enough sleep apps that I expect the 14-day report to show little difference, so I doubt I'd end up paying.
